llm.summary: WS achieved clean liftoff and outperformed SPY, with company-specific alpha recorded as the driver. Materials and metals exposure remain viable competing explanations because no peer or commodity controls were supplied.
llm.root_cause: WS achieved clean liftoff and outperformed SPY, with company-specific alpha recorded as the driver. Materials and metals exposure remain viable competing explanations because no peer or commodity controls were supplied.
llm.lesson: The watch book surfaced WS, while the company-alpha and Materials-cycle books need attribution separating issuer execution from commodity beta.
llm.engines_credit: The watch book was the discovery role model; the company-alpha, Materials-rotation, macro, and catalyst organs lack enough evidence for causal credit.

causal_chain.mechanism: The supplied outcome taxonomy identifies issuer-specific alpha as the main cause.
causal_chain.counterfactual: If WS tracked metals and Materials peers, commodity or sector beta would supersede the issuer-specific explanation.

causal_chain.mechanism: Commodity, industrial-demand, or currency conditions may have transmitted a macro tailwind through Materials exposure.
causal_chain.counterfactual: Persistent peer-adjusted return after commodity and macro controls would favor company alpha.

alternate_explanations: Metals-price strength may have driven the outcome.
Materials-sector rotation may explain part of the relative gain.
An issuer-specific contract, transaction, or operating update may have acted as a catalyst.

signal_hypotheses.measurement: Compare WS pre-entry and subsequent performance with relevant metals, currency, sector, and peer benchmarks.
signal_hypotheses.expected_direction: Positive residual strength should identify issuer-specific alpha beyond commodity beta.
signal_hypotheses.falsifier: Commodity and peer controls explain the return without a meaningful residual.
